column1: # Go≡Rust equivalence-mode OVERRIDES — overrides-on-top-of-DERIVED.
# The equiv mode is DERIVED from example_shape by `equiv_mode` in lib/examples.sh
# (cli→stdout, server→body, live→scenario, tui→pty, webview/fyne/Go-FFI→none).
# Derivation guarantees coverage, so an author-added example AUTO-CLASSIFIES with
# no line here. This file is ONLY exceptions: an example whose derived mode is
# wrong (a non-deterministic cli, a known divergence parked as a finding, a
# Rust-FFI app with no Go reference). Listed here, the mode in column 2 wins.
# Format:  <basename>  <mode>  <reason>
#   <basename>  the example dir basename (e.g. 35-composite-generics, skyshop-rs).
#   <mode>      none | stdout | body | scenario | pty (the override mode).
#   <reason>    why the derived mode is overridden (free text to end of line).
# There is NO forced-full-coverage gate (derivation guarantees coverage). The
# only sanity note: keep this list SMALL — most examples need no override.
# 00-standard-libs is DELIBERATELY NOT overridden: its derived mode is `stdout`,
# so examples-sweep tries the Go reference build, it FAILS (upstream v0.16.29 Go
# codegen emits `undefined: T1` at main.go — memory: upstream-v0-16-29-go-t1-
# regression), and the sweep auto-reports amber `go-ref-broken` — honestly
# surfacing the upstream Go bug live, and auto-flipping back to `equiv-stdout` the
# moment upstream fixes T1 (no manual .tsv edit needed). FINDING #2.

07-todo-cli        none   Std.Log format gap CLOSED (task #5): Rust's Log.* now emits Go's exact `TIMESTAMP LEVEL message` plain line + matching JSON shape (plain + json verified byte-identical to Go after timestamp-normalize). Still pinned `none` PURELY because the RFC3339Nano timestamp the banner prints is non-deterministic by nature — the stdout determinism auto-probe would false-DIFFER on it. NOT a Log.* parity gap any more.
# ── Non-deterministic cli — derived `stdout` would false-DIFFER ──────────────

35-composite-generics   none   non-deterministic cli: prints a Time.now `Generated at` timestamp AND Dict.toList iteration order differs between backends. The stdout determinism auto-probe would catch the timestamp, but pin it here so the intent is explicit.

02-go-stdlib       none   non-deterministic cli: prints a wall-clock `Current time:` (HH:MM:SS) AND makes a live HTTP call whose body length varies — a Go-stdlib-FFI demo with no stable Rust-comparable stdout. The stdout determinism auto-probe USUALLY flags it, but sub-second time stability can fool the 2-probe window into a false DIFFER; pin `none` so it is deterministically excluded.
# ── Rust-FFI app — no Go reference exists to compare against ──────────────────

skyshop-rs         none   examples/rust/skyshop-rs — Rust-FFI app (firestore/stripe/firebase wrapper crates, target=rust); does NOT build on Go — nothing to compare. examples-sweep builds+runs it on Rust alone.
